summary: ModGauge is a 183-line Curve-style liquidity gauge: users stake an LP token, a MasterChef-style accumulator (accRewardPerShare over `working` balances) streams `rewardPerSecond` of a reward token, and a wired ModVoteEscrow lifts each staker's working balance from 40% to 100% of their deposit (the 2.5x boost) in proportion to their share of total ve. The core accumulator math is correct (rewardDebt is always re-based on the same `working` that earned it, so no underflow; overflow needs an absurd rate), the 2.5x cap holds, unstake() and claim() push tokens after state is settled, and LP principal is never touched by the owner. The worst things found are (1) `fund()` is permissionless and rewrites `periodFinish` without checkpointing, so anyone can halt emissions with `fund(0, 1)` and later re-extend to capture the paused gap as a lump sum; (2) working balances are snapshotted against the live, flash-movable `totalStaked` and `kick()` may be called on anyone at any time, so a dust ve lock plus one transaction of borrowed LP buys a permanent 2.5x boost, and a whale can grind every competitor down toward 1x; (3) if the reward token is the staking token, `claim()` pays other stakers' principal. None of these require the owner to misbehave. As-is the block is not safe for real value: deploy it only with distinct stake/reward tokens, an owner-only funding path, and a keeper that kicks stale positions, and treat every emission figure as a promise the contract does not enforce.

findings.title: fund() is permissionless and rewrites periodFinish without checkpointing: anyone can halt emissions, and whoever re-extends the period captures the paused gap retroactively
findings.detail: `fund(amount, duration)` has no access control and no minimum amount; `rewardToken.pull(msg.sender, 0)` succeeds on ERC20Base and most tokens, so any address can set `periodFinish = block.timestamp + duration` for any duration. Because `_effectiveNow()` clamps accrual at `periodFinish`, `fund(0, 1)` freezes emissions one second later and nothing the owner does (setRewardRate, another fund) survives a follow-up `fund(0, 1)`. Worse, `fund()` does not call `_update()` before moving `periodFinish`. `lastUpdate` only advances when someone touches the gauge, so whenever the period is extended after a stretch in which emissions were off (attacker-imposed or a naturally expired schedule), the very next `_update()` accrues `rewardPerSecond` over the entire `lastUpdate -> now` span, including the dead gap, and hands it to whoever is staked at that moment. The rate, the duration and the funded balance are never reconciled with each other (see GAUGE-5), so the retroactive lump is paid out of whatever tokens happen to sit in the contract.
findings.exploit: 1. Owner deploys with rewardPerSecond = 0.05e18, calls fund(1_000_000e18, 30 days) so periodFinish = T+30d; 1,000 LP are staked by honest users. 2. Attacker calls fund(0, 1): periodFinish = T+1. From T+1 on, every _update() pins nowT to T+1 and no one earns anything; honest claims pay one second of emissions. 3. At T+20d the attacker stakes 9,000 LP (stake() runs _update() first, which is a no-op since lastUpdate == periodFinish; the attacker now holds 90% of workingSupply). 4. Attacker calls fund(0, 365 days): periodFinish = T+20d+365d, lastUpdate still T+1. 5. Attacker calls claim(): _update() accrues (20d - 1s) * 0.05e18 = 86,400 tokens into accRewardPerShare over a workingSupply the attacker dominates; attacker receives ~77,760 tokens that the honest 1,000 LP would have earned over those 20 days, paid from the owner's 1,000,000 deposit. 6. Repeat: fund(0, 1) again, wait, stake, extend, claim. Honest variant (no attacker): the 30-day period expires, the gauge is idle for 60 days, the owner re-funds with fund(amount, 30 days); the next touch accrues 60 dead days at once and the fresh deposit is claimable in seconds by whoever was staked.
findings.recommendation: Make `fund()` (or at least the `duration` write) `onlyOwner`, call `_update()` before changing `periodFinish`, and adopt the Synthetix `notifyRewardAmount` pattern: `rewardPerSecond = (amount + leftover) / duration` derived from the deposit, with `require(rewardToken.balanceOf(this) >= rewardPerSecond * duration)`. If permissionless top-ups are desired, let them add balance only and never touch the schedule. Also set `lastUpdate = block.timestamp` whenever the period is restarted so a dead gap can never be back-paid.

findings.title: Working balances snapshot against a flash-movable totalStaked and kick() is unrestricted: a dust ve lock plus borrowed LP buys a permanent 2.5x, and a whale can grind competitors down toward 1x
findings.where: workingBalanceFor() L81-L89, _reboost() L112-L119, kick() L147-L152, stake()/unstake() L121-L143
findings.detail: The boost term is `totalStaked * escrow.balanceOf(user) / veTotal` evaluated at the instant a position is re-based, and the result is stored in `p.working` until that user is next touched. `totalStaked` is a live global that any address can inflate or deflate within one transaction (stake then unstake; ModAMM LP can be minted against flash-borrowed reserves from ModFlashLender and burned again in the same call). Curve guards this by only allowing a third party to kick a user whose ve has changed or expired and by recomputing a user's limit only on that user's own deposit/withdraw; here `kick(anyone)` recomputes at will. Two directions follow: (a) inflate `totalStaked` with temporary LP, kick a colluding address whose ve share is tiny, and its 60% term overshoots its deposit so it is capped at the full 2.5x; unwind the LP and the 2.5x stays frozen in `p.working` until someone else kicks it, at which point the attack is simply re-run. (b) A staker holding most of the pool unstakes, kicks every ve-boosted competitor against the shrunken `totalStaked` (their 60% term collapses), and restakes in the same transaction with their own boost intact. Both raise the attacker's fraction of `workingSupply` and therefore of every emitted token; the cost is gas plus a flash fee.
findings.exploit: Direction (a): pool has totalStaked = 1,000 LP, ve totalSupply = 10,000. Attacker address A locks 1 token for one week in the escrow (balanceOf(A) ~ 1/208 = 0.0048, share s = 4.8e-7) and stakes 100 LP; workingBalanceFor(A) = 40 + 0.6 * 1,100 * 4.8e-7 ~ 40 (1x). In one transaction address B: flashLoan both AMM reserves from ModFlashLender -> addLiquidity -> ~1e9 LP -> stake(1e9) so totalStaked ~ 1e9 -> kick(A): boosted = 40 + 0.6 * 1e9 * 4.8e-7 = 328 > 100, capped to 100 -> A.working = 100 (2.5x) -> B.unstake(1e9) -> removeLiquidity -> repay. A now earns at 2.5x indefinitely with a one-token lock that expires in a week; A.withdraw() on the escrow does not touch the gauge. Direction (b): whale W stakes 90% of T; victim V has 5% of T with enough ve for 2.5x (working = a). W: unstake(all) -> T' = 0.1T -> kick(V): 0.4a + 0.6 * 0.1T * s_V with s_V = 0.1 gives 0.02T + 0.006T = 0.026T < a = 0.05T, V drops to ~1.3x -> W.stake(all) again with W's own working recomputed against the full T. V's share of emissions roughly halves until V notices and re-kicks, and W can repeat every block.
findings.recommendation: Restrict `kick(user)` to the cases Curve allows: the user's escrow lock has expired/decayed to zero (`escrow.balanceOf(user) == 0`, or read `locks(user).end < block.timestamp` from ModVoteEscrow) or the user's ve changed since their last checkpoint; let users re-base themselves only through their own stake/unstake/claim. Add a per-user `lastStakeBlock` and `require(block.number > lastStakeBlock[msg.sender])` in unstake() so LP cannot be flash-staked within one transaction. Consider re-basing every touched user against a `totalStaked` checkpointed at the previous block rather than the live value.

findings.title: If rewardToken == stakeToken, claim() pays rewards out of other stakers' LP principal
findings.where: claim() L154-L166 (available = rewardToken.balanceOf(address(this)) L161), constructor L57-L60
findings.detail: The constructor only rejects the zero address; nothing stops the same ERC20 being wired to both the `stakeToken` and `rewardToken` ports, and 'stake X, earn X' is a natural graph to draw. `claim()` treats the contract's entire balance of `rewardToken` as claimable, and when that token is also the staked asset the balance is mostly other people's principal. Because emissions accrue with no funding check (GAUGE-5), rewards are always 'earned' whether or not anyone funded them, so the first claimers walk away with deposits and later `unstake()` calls revert with PUSH_FAILED.
findings.exploit: 1. Deploy ModGauge with stakeToken_ = rewardToken_ = MOD, rewardPerSecond_ = 0.05e18 (catalog default), never call fund(). 2. Alice stakes 1,000 MOD, Bob stakes 1,000 MOD. 3. One day later Alice's earned() = 0.05 * 86,400 / 2 = 2,160 MOD; she calls claim(): available = 2,000 (all of it principal), so she receives 2,000 MOD. 4. Bob calls unstake(1000): stakeToken.push reverts (balance 0). Bob has lost his deposit; Alice has both. No owner action or exotic token was needed.
findings.recommendation: `require(stakeToken_ != rewardToken_, "SAME_TOKEN")` in the constructor, and defensively compute `available = rewardToken.balanceOf(this) - (rewardToken == stakeToken ? totalStaked : 0)`. Have the planner refuse to wire the same node to both ports.

findings.title: Owner can freeze every staked LP token by pointing escrow at an address whose reads revert; setEscrow is unchecked and re-bases nobody
findings.where: setEscrow() L180-L182, workingBalanceFor() L84-L87, _reboost() L112-L119, unstake() L133-L143
findings.detail: `stake()`, `unstake()` and `kick()` all call `_reboost()`, which calls `escrow.totalSupply()` and `escrow.balanceOf()` whenever `escrow != 0`. `setEscrow()` accepts any address with no interface check and no `_update()`. If the owner sets an EOA, a self-destructed contract, or any contract without those functions, every high-level call reverts and all three entry points are bricked; only `claim()` still works, so principal is frozen until the same owner reverses the change. The default `owner_` is the deploying wallet, so this is one EOA signature. A malicious-but-functional escrow is a softer version: the owner can grant any address 100% of 've' and take a 2.5x share while honest lockers keep their old `working` until kicked, and honest lockers are then kicked down to 1x.
findings.exploit: 1. Users stake 100,000 LP into a gauge wired to ModVoteEscrow. 2. Owner calls setEscrow(0x000...dEaD) (or any EOA). 3. Any user's unstake(): _reboost() -> workingBalanceFor() -> escrow.totalSupply() reverts (call to non-contract fails the extcodesize check). stake() and kick() revert the same way. 4. LP is locked; only claim() proceeds. Owner alone can undo it. Variant: owner deploys a FakeEscrow whose balanceOf(owner) == totalSupply(), calls setEscrow(fake), kick(owner) to lift itself to 2.5x, then kick(each honest ve holder) to drop them to 1x.
findings.recommendation: Validate in setEscrow (staticcall `totalSupply()` and `balanceOf(address(0))` via try/catch and revert on failure), or make `escrow` immutable. Wrap the escrow reads in `_reboost()` with try/catch that falls back to the 40% base so unstake() can never depend on an external call succeeding. Wire the `governor` port to a ModTimelock/ModGovernor so escrow changes are delayed and public.

findings.title: Emissions accrue with no backing and claim() is first-come-first-served: rate, duration and balance are never reconciled, late claimers starve, and excess funding is unrecoverable
findings.where: constructor L61, _update() L73-L75, claim() L160-L163, fund() L170-L173, setRewardRate() L175-L178
findings.detail: `rewardPerSecond` is set in the constructor (catalog default 0.05e18/s ~ 4,320 tokens/day) and starts accruing at deploy with a zero balance; `fund()` adds tokens without touching the rate and `setRewardRate()` changes the rate without checking the balance. `earned()` therefore reports a promise, and `claim()` silently pays `min(pending, balance)`, keeping the remainder as `pending` with no obligation on anyone to ever fund it. Whoever claims first takes the whole balance; everyone after gets zero and a growing IOU. There is also no owner sweep, so tokens deposited beyond what the schedule ever emits (e.g. `fund(amount, 0)` after periodFinish has passed, which restarts nothing) are stuck forever. With `periodFinish == 0` (the state after the composer deploys, since fund is a post-deploy wire) emissions run unbounded.
findings.exploit: 1. Deploy with rewardPerSecond = 0.05e18; owner calls fund(100_000e18, 30 days). 2. Ten users stake 100 LP each (equal working balances). 3. After 30 days total promised = 129,600 tokens, 12,960 each. 4. Users 1-7 claim 12,960 each (90,720 out); user 8 claims and receives the remaining 9,280 (pending keeps 3,680); users 9 and 10 receive 0 with 12,960 pending each. Nothing forces the owner to top up. Variant: owner calls setRewardRate(10e18) by mistake; the gauge now 'owes' 864,000 tokens/day against whatever it holds.
findings.recommendation: Derive the rate from funding (Synthetix `notifyRewardAmount`): `fund(amount, duration)` sets `rewardPerSecond = (amount + leftover) / duration` and `periodFinish`. Track `rewardsOwed` (sum of pending + unclaimed accumulator) and require `balance >= owed + rate * remaining` in setRewardRate. Add an owner `sweepExcess()` limited to `balance - owed - rate * remaining` so over-funding is recoverable without ever touching promised rewards. Treat `earned()` as an estimate in the UI.

findings.title: Boosts never refresh on their own: an expired or decayed lock keeps its 2.5x until someone pays gas to kick it, and nobody is paid to
findings.where: _reboost() L112-L119, kick() L147-L152, stake() L121-L131; veescrow.sol balanceOf() L58-L62, createLock() L122-L134
findings.detail: `p.working` is only recomputed inside the user's own stake/unstake or a third-party kick(); claim() deliberately does not re-base. ve weight in ModVoteEscrow decays linearly every second and reaches zero at the (week-rounded) lock end, so a boost fixed at lock creation over-earns continuously and then fully after expiry. ModVoteEscrow allows a lock as short as the next week boundary, so the cheapest route to a lasting 2.5x is a one-week lock on a fresh, low-ve deployment, followed by never touching the gauge. `kick()` is free to call but carries no bounty, so on a small pool nobody runs the keeper and every stale boost is paid for by the honest stakers' share. The catalog docs say 'anyone can kick() a wallet whose lock expired' as if that were self-executing; it is not.
findings.exploit: 1. New deployment: veTotal small (say 500 ve). 2. Attacker locks 104,000 tokens for one week: ve = 104,000 * 1/208 = 500, share 50%. 3. Attacker stakes LP equal to 25% of the pool: 60% term = 0.6 * T * 0.5 = 0.3T > 0.25T, capped to full deposit, 2.5x. 4. One week later the lock expires; attacker calls escrow.withdraw() (does not touch the gauge) and recovers all 104,000 tokens. 5. `p.working` still equals the full deposit; the attacker keeps earning 2.5x for months unless a stranger spends gas on kick(attacker), after which the attacker relocks for a week and repeats.
findings.recommendation: Pay kickers: transfer a slice (e.g. 1-5%) of the kicked user's settled `pending` to `msg.sender` when the kick actually lowers `working`. Re-base the caller inside claim() so at least self-touches refresh. Have ModVoteEscrow expose `locks(user).end` and let the gauge apply base-only boost once `end <= block.timestamp` without waiting for a kick. Document that boosts are 'as of last touch' and run a keeper that kicks every boosted position weekly.

findings.title: stake() pulls the LP token between _settle() and _reboost(): a hook-bearing stake token can reenter claim()/kick() and be credited twice
findings.detail: `stake()` calls `_settle(p)` (adds `working * acc / 1e18 - rewardDebt` to `pending`) and only later, in `_reboost()`, resets `rewardDebt`. Between those two lines it makes an external call (`stakeToken.pull`). If the staking token invokes the sender/recipient during `transferFrom` (ERC777, ERC20 with hooks, a malicious paste-in address), the callback can call `claim()` or `kick(self)`, whose `_settle` adds the same delta a second time before `rewardDebt` is reset, and `claim()` pays it out. The catalog's ModAMM/ModToken LP tokens have no hooks, so this is latent for graphs built purely from the catalog, but it becomes a repeatable reward drain (2x fair share on every stake) for any external token wired into the `stakeToken` port. unstake() and claim() are ordered correctly.
findings.exploit: 1. Gauge deployed with an ERC777-style LP token. 2. Attacker stakes, waits until earned() = 1,000. 3. Attacker calls stake(1): _update(), _settle(p) -> pending = 1,000 -> pull() fires tokensToSend on the attacker's contract -> callback calls claim(): _settle adds another 1,000 (rewardDebt unchanged), rewardDebt reset, 2,000 transferred out -> control returns, p.amount += 1, _reboost resets rewardDebt. 4. Attacker collected 2,000 for 1,000 earned; repeat on every accrual interval.
findings.recommendation: Add a `nonReentrant` guard to stake/unstake/claim/kick, and reorder stake() so the pull happens before `_settle` (or settle and re-base in one step after the transfer). Treat the `stakeToken` port as untrusted.

findings.title: Fee-on-transfer or rebasing stake tokens break unstake accounting; surplus from positive rebases is stuck
findings.detail: `stake()` credits `p.amount += amount` and `totalStaked += amount` by the requested figure, not the balance actually received, and `unstake()` pushes the recorded figure back. With a fee-on-transfer token the contract holds less than `totalStaked` and the last unstakers revert with PUSH_FAILED; with a negative-rebase token the same; with a positive-rebase token the excess belongs to nobody and there is no sweep. ModAMM LP tokens are plain ERC20Base and are unaffected; the risk is any external token pasted into the `stakeToken` port.
findings.exploit: 1. Wire a 1% fee-on-transfer token as stakeToken. 2. Alice stakes 100 (contract receives 99, records 100); Bob stakes 100 (198 held, 200 recorded). 3. Alice unstakes 100: succeeds, 98 left. 4. Bob unstakes 100: PUSH_FAILED; Bob can only recover 98 and must guess the amount.
findings.recommendation: Measure `balanceBefore/After` around the pull and credit the delta; document that rebasing tokens are unsupported, or add an owner-only `skim()` that transfers `balanceOf(this) - totalStaked` (never more) to a sink.

findings.title: Each stake/unstake/kick pays for the escrow's week-walk: up to 208 cold SLOADs if nobody has checkpointed ModVoteEscrow recently; precision is fine at catalog defaults
findings.where: workingBalanceFor() L85-L87; veescrow.sol totalSupply() L65-L82, checkpoint() L86-L100
findings.detail: `ModVoteEscrow.totalSupply()` walks from `lastPoint` week by week up to 208 iterations, reading `slopeChanges[next]` each time (~2,100 gas cold), so a gauge action after months of escrow inactivity can cost ~450k extra gas; it does not revert and any escrow lock/withdraw or `checkpoint()` resets it. On the accumulator: `dt * rewardPerSecond * 1e18 / workingSupply` overflows only for rates above ~1e59 wei/s and truncates to zero only when `workingSupply > rewardPerSecond * 1e18` (a 1 wei/s rate against 1e18 wei of working balance), neither reachable with the 0.05e18 default. `boostBps()` returns 0 for positions whose 40% base rounds to 0 (deposits below 3 wei).
findings.exploit: 1. Escrow untouched for 100 weeks. 2. A user's unstake() triggers totalSupply() which loops 100 times before returning; the transaction costs ~250k gas more than expected but succeeds. Calling escrow.checkpoint() first brings it back to normal.
findings.recommendation: Run `escrow.checkpoint()` in the keeper that kicks stale positions. Keep rewardPerSecond in the 1e12-1e24 range. No code change required.

safe_use: Never wire the same token to `LP token` and `Reward token`: claim() will pay rewards out of other stakers' deposits and later unstakes will revert. Use a separate emissions token, or the ModStaking block for single-asset staking.

fund() is public: anyone can call fund(0, 1) and stop emissions, and anyone who later extends the period collects the gap retroactively. Until fund() is gated, keep `periodFinish` at 0 (never pass a duration) and control emissions with setRewardRate() only, accepting that the schedule then has no end date.

Fund before the first stake and keep `rewardToken.balanceOf(gauge) >= rewardPerSecond * seconds_remaining` at all times; the contract will happily promise rewards it does not hold, and claims are first-come-first-served. Over-funded tokens cannot be recovered, so fund in tranches.

Boosts are snapshots: they do not refresh when a lock decays or expires, and kick() has no bounty. Run a keeper (cron) that calls escrow.checkpoint() then kick(user) for every boosted position at least weekly, or expect expired locks to keep earning 2.5x.

A dust ve lock plus one transaction of borrowed LP can buy a permanent 2.5x for a colluding address, and a large staker can kick competitors against a temporarily shrunken pool. Do not deploy a ModFlashLender over either AMM reserve of the LP you gauge, and treat boost as advisory on small pools.

setEscrow() is one owner signature away from freezing every unstake (any non-escrow address bricks _reboost). Wire the `governor` port to a ModTimelock/ModGovernor before real liquidity arrives, and never point escrow at anything but a live ModVoteEscrow; setEscrow(address(0)) is the safe 'boost off' setting.

Only plain ERC20s (ModAMM LP, ModToken) belong on the `LP token` port: hook-bearing tokens open a double-settle in stake(), and fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens leave the last unstakers unable to withdraw.
earned() and boostBps() report the schedule, not the balance; show users `min(earned, rewardToken.balanceOf(gauge))` as the claimable figure.
